## 1. Purpose

Protect technicians from the unexpected startup or release of stored energy while servicing equipment at customer sites and in the shop.

## 2. Responsibilities

The qualified technician performing the work applies locks and documents the lockout. For the systems listed in Section 4, a second qualified person acts as verifier.

## 3. Procedure

- Notify the customer contact and affected employees.

- Identify every energy source, including stored pressure and refrigerant charge.

- Shut the equipment down using normal stop controls.

- Isolate each energy source at the disconnect, valve or blind.

- Apply personal locks and tags to each isolation point.

- Release or restrain stored energy.

- Verify zero energy (Section 4 applies to ammonia and high-pressure systems).

- Record the lockout on the LOTO tag log.

- Do the work.

- Restore and sign off on the tag log.

## 1. Purpose

Protect technicians from the unexpected startup or release of stored energy while servicing equipment at customer sites and in the shop.

## 2. Responsibilities

The qualified technician performing the work applies locks and documents the lockout. For the systems listed in Section 4, a second qualified person acts as verifier.

## 3. Procedure

- Notify the customer contact and affected employees.

- Identify every energy source, including stored pressure and refrigerant charge.

- Shut the equipment down using normal stop controls.

- Isolate each energy source at the disconnect, valve or blind.

- Apply personal locks and tags to each isolation point.

- Release or restrain stored energy.

- Verify zero energy (Section 4 applies to ammonia and high-pressure systems).

- Record the lockout on the LOTO tag log.

- Do the work.

- Restore and sign off on the tag log.

## Hot Job (Emergency Service) Policy

Version 2 Effective January 1, 2025 Replaces the March 2018 policy

## 1. Hot Job definition

A Hot Job is any call where the customer requests a response the same day, or outside 7:00 am to 4:00 pm Monday through Friday. Weekend and holiday calls are always Hot Jobs.

## 2. Billing

All hours are billed at 1.5x the standard rate plus a $250 dispatch fee. Parts are billed at Blue Book markup.

## 3. Coding

The dispatcher codes the work order HOT when the call is taken. Techs may not change the code. Billing invoices HOT work orders with the 1.5x rate and the dispatch fee line.

## 4. Exceptions

No exceptions without written approval from Dave Brennan or Sarah Okafor.

## Approved

D. Brennan

## Hot Job (Emergency Service) Policy

Version 2 Effective January 1, 2025 Replaces the March 2018 policy

## 1. Hot Job definition

A Hot Job is any call where the customer requests a response the same day, or outside 7:00 am to 4:00 pm Monday through Friday. Weekend and holiday calls are always Hot Jobs.

## 2. Billing

All hours are billed at 1.5x the standard rate plus a $250 dispatch fee. Parts are billed at Blue Book markup.

## 3. Coding

The dispatcher codes the work order HOT when the call is taken. Techs may not change the code. Billing invoices HOT work orders with the 1.5x rate and the dispatch fee line.

## 4. Exceptions

No exceptions without written approval from Dave Brennan or Sarah Okafor.

## Approved

## Hot Job (Emergency Service) Policy

Version 2 Effective January 1, 2025 Replaces the March 2018 policy

## 1. Hot Job definition

A Hot Job is any call where the customer requests a response the same day, or outside 7:00 am to 4:00 pm Monday through Friday. Weekend and holiday calls are always Hot Jobs.

## 2. Billing

All hours are billed at 1.5x the standard rate plus a $250 dispatch fee. Parts are billed at Blue Book markup.

## 3. Coding

The dispatcher codes the work order HOT when the call is taken. Techs may not change the code. Billing invoices HOT work orders with the 1.5x rate and the dispatch fee line.

## 4. Exceptions

No exceptions without written approval from Dave Brennan or Sarah Okafor.

## Approved

D. Brennan

Andrea Reyes, Branch Manager, Columbus. July 14, 2025.

Our coding has not been consistent. Starting today, every call goes through this checklist before the work order is saved.

- Did the customer ask for someone the same day? If yes: HOT.

- Is it before 7:00 am, after 4:00 pm, a weekend or a holiday? If yes: HOT.

- Is it a scheduled repair the customer is fine waiting on? Then T&M.

## Columbus Branch - Hot Job Coding Checklist

Andrea Reyes, Branch Manager, Columbus. July 14, 2025.

Our coding has not been consistent. Starting today, every call goes through this checklist before the work order is saved.

- Did the customer ask for someone the same day? If yes: HOT.

- Is it before 7:00 am, after 4:00 pm, a weekend or a holiday? If yes: HOT.

- Is it a scheduled repair the customer is fine waiting on? Then T&M.

- Not sure? Code it HOT and flag it for me. I will review every flagged call daily.

- Never change a HOT code to T&M after the fact without my written OK.

### Why

Hot Jobs bill at 1.5x plus the dispatch fee. If we code them as T&M we do the same work for less money and the customer never knows the difference. I review a sample of last week's tickets every Monday and post the results on the board.
